question.knowledge_point: Computing a Conditional Probability Over an Interval
question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | $Y=6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.25$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0$ |

Compute $P(2<Y\le 6\,|\,X=0)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<Y\le 6\,|\,X=0) & =\frac{P((2<Y\le 6),X=0)}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,(2<Y\le 6))}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,Y=4)+P(X=0,Y=6)}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(0,6)}{{f}_{X}(0)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(0) & =f(0,0)+f(0,2)+f(0,4)+f(0,6) \\  & =0.25+0.05+0.1+0 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(0,4)=0.1$ and $f(0,6)=0.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<Y\le 6\,|\,X=0) & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(0,6)}{{f}_{X}(0)} \\  & =\frac{0.1+0}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.4} \\  & =0.25.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | $Y=6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{18}$ | $\frac{5}{18}$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{18}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |

Compute $P(2\le Y\le 6\,|\,X=2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(2\le Y\le 6\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{P((2\le Y\le 6),X=2)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,(2\le Y\le 6))}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,Y=2)+P(X=2,Y=4)+P(X=2,Y=6)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{f(2,2)+f(2,4)+f(2,6)}{{f}_{X}(2)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(2) & =f(2,0)+f(2,2)+f(2,4)+f(2,6) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{18}+0+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,2)=\frac{1}{18},f(2,4)=0$ and $f(2,6)=\frac{1}{6}.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le Y\le 6\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,2)+f(2,4)+f(2,6)}{{f}_{X}(2)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{18}+0+\frac{1}{6})}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2}{9})}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing the Value of a Conditional Probability Mass Function at a Point
question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{5}{27}$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ |
| $X=4$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{8}{27}$ | $\frac{2}{27}$ |

Compute ${f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,1)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.worked_solution:
The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,1)=P(X=4\,|\,Y=1).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=4\,|\,Y=1)=\frac{P(X=4,Y=1)}{P(Y=1)}=\frac{f(4,1)}{{f}_{Y}(1)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(1) & =f(2,1)+f(4,1) \\  & =\frac{5}{27}+\frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{8}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(4,1)=\frac{1}{9}.$ 

Finally, substituting  ${f}_{Y}(1)=\frac{8}{27}$ and $f(4,1)=\frac{1}{9}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,1) & =P(X=4\,|\,Y=1) \\  & =\frac{f(4,1)}{{f}_{Y}(1)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{9})}{(\frac{8}{27})} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |

Compute ${f}_{Y|X}(1\,|\,0)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=x).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(1\,|\,0)=P(Y=1\,|\,X=0).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(Y=1\,|\,X=0)=\frac{P(X=0,Y=1)}{P(X=0)}=\frac{f(0,1)}{{f}_{X}(0)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(0) & =f(0,0)+f(0,1)+f(0,2) \\  & =0.3+0.2+0.1 \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(0,1)=0.2.$ 

Finally, substituting  ${f}_{X}(0)=0.6$ and $f(0,1)=0.2$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(1\,|\,0) & =P(Y=1\,|\,X=0) \\  & =\frac{f(0,1)}{{f}_{X}(0)} \\  & =\frac{0.2}{0.6} \\  & ≈0.33.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
question.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
question.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-x-y-3z=1 \\ 2x+2y+6z=-2 \\ -2x-2y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y+z=2 \\ 0x+y-3z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=-3,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.
